sm: The host says Republicans controlled Texas for about thirty years, but this past Tuesday the governor's race, Senate, lieutenant governor, attorney general and House all flipped to Democrats. He blames mostly Governor Abbott rather than Trump, saying Abbott repeatedly promised to cut property taxes over three terms and never did, so voters stopped believing him. He contrasts Abbott with Ron DeSantis, who he says grew his voter base by twenty percent by governing with courage. He argues Republicans with majorities accomplish little compared with Democrats, and holds up Charlie Kirk as a leader who led from the front. He closes by saying the church is the real problem, citing a claim that Seattle's churchgoers could change its council and a drop in the evangelical vote, and urging Christians to show up.
